title: x.com link never fetched; bot invented the tweet's subject
why: The asker linked a tweet about China moving the yuan onto a gold standard and Hong Kong's gold clearing system. NOTHING in the system can retrieve an x.com URL: no registered tool takes a URL, google_search grounds on question text rather than browsing, code execution has no network, and _maybe_fetch_user_urls skips login-walled hosts and returns an empty string with no signal that content is missing. The model searched, got that day's long-end macro news, and wrote three confident bullets about 30Y Treasury yields and Treasury buybacks, asserting the tweet 'called it a total system collapse because nobody wanted the long-end debt.' Wrong subject entirely, about a document the asker was looking at, with four citations attached and every guard green. Citations on a confabulation are worse than a visibly wrong answer.
